key_insight: LLM2R reformulates 3D part assembly as a single-pass sequence modeling problem, using a pretrained decoder-only LLM to predict all part poses jointly with global context.
engineering_relevance: For fractured or disassembled objects with many parts, this offers a scalable alternative to pairwise or iterative assembly methods, improving accuracy while reducing inference cost.
method: Encode each part with Point-BERT + Q-Former into compact geometric token blocks.
Concatenate all part tokens and process them with a causal LLM adapted via LoRA in one forward pass.
Append learnable summary tokens after the final part so they aggregate whole-assembly context for a part-aware pose head.
evidence_signal: The method reports top performance on PartNet, PartNeXt, and Breaking Bad, with especially large gains as part count increases and strong zero-shot transfer to unseen categories.
watch_item: Because causal attention only exposes earlier parts directly, the approach depends on summary tokens to recover global context, so token design and ordering may affect performance.
paper_title: LLM2R: From Large Language Models to 3D Reassemblers
